headline: Smart ring maker Oura has withdrawn its planned US stock listing, which was meant to raise up to $2.2 billion, days after launching it.
score_reason: Lowered by 1: the withdrawal happened before 4 Oct 2026 and the AI wearables angle of the pool headline could not be verified.
importance_line: What changed is that a popular health-ring maker pulled its share sale, which matters to its investors and staff, then to the wider market for new listings, and the doubt is that Oura gave no reason, so any link to AI wearables or privacy is unconfirmed.
summary: Silicon UK reports that Oura, the smart ring maker, has withdrawn the share sale it launched on 21 September, which was meant to raise up to $2.2 billion at an implied value of $15 billion; Oura gave no reason, and the report points to rising interest rates behind other pulled US listings. CNBC's headline presents the move as part of a stalled breakout for AI wearables, a link Oura has not confirmed.
notes: Exact withdrawal date not stated in Silicon UK; the FOLLOW-UP date is the latest a weekly IPO recap headline suggests and is not confirmed. Pool source CNBC unreadable.
